symbols.role: Latent cellwise direction, including cells on the observable tie face.

symbols.def: The complete fixed-marginal coupling polytope on the observable tie face.

symbols.name: \Gamma_x
symbols.def: The tie-safe partial-transport feasibility set selected by the sign of \(\Delta q(x)\), with a separate zero-gap branch.

symbols.name: B_L(x)
symbols.def: The lower threshold-cut value in cell \(x\).

symbols.name: B_U(x)
symbols.def: The upper threshold-cut value in cell \(x\).

symbols.def: The identified set of \(\theta\) over compatible full laws.

symbols.role: Fixed positive-survivor support at a law \(P\).

symbols.name: \mathbb Z_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}
symbols.def: The joint multinomial Gaussian limit of the finite vector of empirical observed-cell probabilities under \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_L(x)
symbols.def: The set of threshold cuts attaining \(B_L(x)\), including the zero cut.

symbols.name: \mathcal A_U(x)
symbols.def: The set of threshold cuts attaining \(B_U(x)\), including the mass cap.

symbols.name: \widetilde\ell_i(x)
symbols.def: The empirical analogue of \(\ell_i(x)\), with every empirical conditional probability defined as zero when its empirical \(X,Z\) denominator is zero.

symbols.name: \widetilde h_j(x)
symbols.def: The empirical analogue of \(h_j(x)\), with every empirical conditional probability defined as zero when its empirical \(X,Z\) denominator is zero.

symbols.name: \widehat\ell_i(x)
symbols.def: The lower-arm coordinates of \(\widehat c_n\), equivalently \(\widehat\ell_i(x)=\max\{\widetilde\ell_i(x),0\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat h_j(x)
symbols.def: The higher-arm coordinates of \(\widehat c_n\), equivalently \(\widehat h_j(x)=\max\{\widetilde h_j(x),0\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat B_L(x)
symbols.def: The lower threshold-cut value obtained by substituting projected capacities into the positive, negative, or exact-zero branch according to the sign of \(\widehat{\Delta q}(x)\).

symbols.name: \widehat B_U(x)
symbols.def: The upper threshold-cut value obtained by substituting projected capacities into the positive, negative, or exact-zero branch according to the sign of \(\widehat{\Delta q}(x)\).

symbols.name: \widehat r_x
symbols.role: Unconditional estimated cell survivor mass used for screening.

symbols.name: \eta_n
symbols.def: A zero-cell omission threshold satisfying \(\eta_n\downarrow0\) and \(\sqrt n\eta_n\to\infty\).

symbols.def: \(\widehat\Psi_n=(\widehat N_{L,n}/\widehat M_n,\widehat N_{U,n}/\widehat M_n)\) when \(\widehat M_n>0\), and \(\widehat\Psi_n=(0,1)\) when \(\widehat M_n=0\).

assumptions.condition: \(P\{d(x)(S_1-S_0)\ge0\mid C,X=x\}=1\) for every \(x\) with \(P(C\mid X=x)>0\), where \(d(x)\in\{-1,+1\}\).

standard.name: Covariate-specific weak sample-selection monotonicity of Dong and Heiler, Assumption 3.2

assumptions.condition: \(|\Delta q(x)|\ge\kappa_{\sigma}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) with \(p_x>0\) and \(m(x)>0\).

standard.name: Strong sign-separation variant for covariate-specific selection direction

definitions.name: Tie-safe survivor-complier model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M=\{P:P\text{ satisfies conditional instrument independence, treatment and outcome consistency, treatment-mediated selection and outcome exclusion, instrument overlap, no defiers, latent-direction weak selection monotonicity, and positive aggregate survivor-complier mass}\}\).

definitions.name: Direction-separated inference law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n=\{P\in\mathcal M:P\text{ satisfies the direction-separation, uniform aggregate-survivor, and independent-sampling conditions at index }n\}\).

definitions.name: Observable selected-complier capacities
definitions.construction: For \(i,j\in\mathcal Y\), form \(\ell_i(x)\) and \(h_j(x)\) from the two conditional instrument contrasts displayed in the symbol table, set \(q_0(x)=\sum_i\ell_i(x)\), \(q_1(x)=\sum_jh_j(x)\), define \(\Delta q(x)=q_1(x)-q_0(x)\), and set \(m(x)=\min\{q_0(x),q_1(x)\}\).

definitions.name: Tie-safe directional partial-transport polytope
definitions.construction: \[\Gamma_x^{+}=\left\{\gamma_x\ge0:\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x}=\ell_i(x),\;\sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}\le h_j(x)\right\},\qquad \Gamma_x^{-}=\left\{\gamma_x\ge0:\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x}\le\ell_i(x),\;\sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}=h_j(x)\right\},\] \[\Gamma_x^{0}=\left\{\gamma_x\ge0:\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x}=\ell_i(x),\;\sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}=h_j(x)\right\}.\] Define \(\Gamma_x=\Gamma_x^{+}\) if \(\Delta q(x)>0\), \(\Gamma_x=\Gamma_x^{-}\) if \(\Delta q(x)<0\), and \(\Gamma_x=\Gamma_x^{0}\) if \(\Delta q(x)=0\).

definitions.name: Closed threshold-cut endpoints
definitions.construction: If \(\Delta q(x)>0\), define \(B_L(x)=\max\{0,\max_{t\in\mathcal Y}[\ell_{\le t}(x)-h_{\le t}(x)]\}\). If \(\Delta q(x)<0\), define \(B_L(x)=\max\{0,\max_{t\in\mathcal Y}[h_{>t}(x)-\ell_{>t}(x)]\}\). If \(\Delta q(x)=0\), define the explicit tie branch \(B_L(x)=\max\{0,\max_{t\in\mathcal Y}[\ell_{\le t}(x)-h_{\le t}(x)]\}\). In every branch define \(B_U(x)=\min\{m(x),\min_{t\in\mathcal Y}[\ell_{<t}(x)+h_{>t}(x)]\}\).

definitions.name: Threshold-flow and latent-completion construction
definitions.construction: Build, in each cell, the bipartite network with source capacities given by the required row submargin, sink capacities given by the required column submargin, and benefit arcs \(i\to j\) exactly when \(i<j\). Use nested threshold cuts to compute the extremal benefit flow, fill the complementary nonbenefit arcs greedily in outcome order, and allocate every residual selected-complier mass to the one-sided selection stratum before adjoining arbitrary never-taker and always-taker components that reproduce the remaining observed cells.

definitions.name: Fully specified three-level observed and latent witness
definitions.construction: Let \(X=x^{\star}\) almost surely, \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star}(Z=1)=P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star}(Z=0)=1/2\), and \(K=3\). Given \(Z=0\), assign probabilities \(0.075\), \(0.10\), and \(0.075\) to \((D,S,Y)=(0,1,0),(0,1,1),(0,1,2)\), respectively, and probability \(0.75\) to \((D,S,Y)=(0,0,\star)\). Given \(Z=1\), assign probabilities \(0.10\), \(0.25\), and \(0.15\) to \((D,S,Y)=(1,1,0),(1,1,1),(1,1,2)\), respectively, and probability \(0.50\) to \((D,S,Y)=(1,0,\star)\); all unlisted conditional cells have probability zero. Construct \(P^{\star}\) by taking every unit to satisfy \(D_0=0,D_1=1\), allocating masses \(0.075,0.10,0.075\) to \(S_0=S_1=1\) with diagonal survivor pairs \((Y_0,Y_1)=(0,0),(1,1),(2,2)\), allocating mass \(0.25\) to \(S_0=0,S_1=1\) with \(Y_1\) residual masses \((0.025,0.15,0.075)\), and allocating mass \(0.50\) to \(S_0=S_1=0\). Take \(Z\) independent with probability one half and assign arbitrary latent outcomes wherever selection makes them unobserved.

definitions.name: Total constrained plug-in endpoint estimator
definitions.construction: For every empirical conditional probability given \((X=x,Z=z)\), use its empirical ratio when the denominator is positive and the fixed value zero when the denominator is zero. Form \(\widetilde c_n=(\widetilde\ell,\widetilde h)\), set \(\mathfrak C=\prod_{x\in\mathcal X}\mathbb R_+^{2K}\), and define \(\widehat c_n=\Pi_{\mathfrak C}(\widetilde c_n)=\arg\min_{c\in\mathfrak C}\|c-\widetilde c_n\|_2^2\). The fixed Euclidean metric makes the minimizer unique, and \(\Pi_{\mathfrak C}\) is the coordinatewise positive-part map. From \(\widehat c_n=(\widehat\ell,\widehat h)\), form \(\widehat q_0(x)=\sum_i\widehat\ell_i(x)\), \(\widehat q_1(x)=\sum_j\widehat h_j(x)\), \(\widehat{\Delta q}(x)=\widehat q_1(x)-\widehat q_0(x)\), and \(\widehat m(x)=\min\{\widehat q_0(x),\widehat q_1(x)\}\). Evaluate \(\widehat B_L(x),\widehat B_U(x)\) by the positive branch if \(\widehat{\Delta q}(x)>0\), the negative branch if it is negative, and the explicit tie branch if it is zero. Set \(\widehat r_x=\widehat p_x\widehat m(x)\), retain exactly the cells satisfying \(\widehat r_x>\eta_n\), and form \(\widehat M_n=\sum_x\mathbf 1\{\widehat r_x>\eta_n\}\widehat p_x\widehat m(x)\), \(\widehat N_{L,n}=\sum_x\mathbf 1\{\widehat r_x>\eta_n\}\widehat p_x\widehat B_L(x)\), and \(\widehat N_{U,n}=\sum_x\mathbf 1\{\widehat r_x>\eta_n\}\widehat p_x\widehat B_U(x)\). Define \(\widehat\Psi_n=(\widehat N_{L,n}/\widehat M_n,\widehat N_{U,n}/\widehat M_n)\) when \(\widehat M_n>0\), and use the fixed fallback \(\widehat\Psi_n=(0,1)\) otherwise.

definitions.name: Near-active-face directional-multiplier handle
definitions.construction: Use the same retained-cell rule \(\widehat r_x>\eta_n\), localize all threshold cuts within \(a_n\) of each estimated optimum, retain the coordinatewise nonnegativity faces generated by \(\Pi_{\mathfrak C}\), apply those estimated faces to \(\mathbb G_n^{\xi}\), and propagate the two endpoint perturbations through the screened common-denominator quotient. The target object is a data-dependent critical region \(\mathcal C_{1-\alpha,n}\) for simultaneous coverage; the rates for \(a_n\) and \(\eta_n\), critical-value calibration, uniform face recovery, and any local-to-zero direction-gap extension are to be determined.

statements.statement: For every supported \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(i,j\in\mathcal Y\), \(\ell_i(x)=P(Y_0=i,S_0=1,C\mid X=x)\) and \(h_j(x)=P(Y_1=j,S_1=1,C\mid X=x)\). Hence \(\Delta q(x)=P(S_1=1,C\mid X=x)-P(S_0=1,C\mid X=x)\) and, under weak selection monotonicity, \(m(x)=P(S_0=S_1=1,C\mid X=x)\). If \(\Delta q(x)>0\), then \(d(x)=+1\); if \(\Delta q(x)<0\), then \(d(x)=-1\). No direction is identified from the observable gap when \(\Delta q(x)=0\).
statements.justification: This projection converts observed IV contrasts into the two latent submargins needed for transport.
statements.gap: KennedyHarrisKeele2019 targets a survivor-complier mean, and DongHeiler2026 Assumption 3.2 with equations (3.1)--(3.2) partitions weak selection directions for trimmed mean bounds; neither identifies the two ordinal submeasures as capacities for a same-unit coupling.
statements.consumer: An analyst can compute the survivor-complier outcome capacities directly from the Job Corps instrument, treatment, employment, and categorized-wage cells.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a cell \(x\) with \(p_x>0\).  Instrument overlap makes both conditional laws below well defined.  By treatment consistency, selection exclusion-consistency, and outcome exclusion-consistency,
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}(Y=i,S=1,D=0\mid Z=z,X=x)
 =P(Y_0=i,S_0=1,D_z=0\mid Z=z,X=x).
\]
Conditional instrument independence removes \(Z=z\) from the right-hand side.  Therefore, using no defiers so that \(\{D_1=0\}\subseteq\{D_0=0\}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\ell_i(x)
&=P(Y_0=i,S_0=1,D_0=0\mid X=x)
  -P(Y_0=i,S_0=1,D_1=0\mid X=x)\\
&=P(Y_0=i,S_0=1,D_0=0,D_1=1\mid X=x)\\
&=P(Y_0=i,S_0=1,C\mid X=x).
\end{aligned}
\]
The symmetric calculation, now using \(\{D_0=1\}\subseteq\{D_1=1\}\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
h_j(x)
&=P(Y_1=j,S_1=1,D_1=1\mid X=x)
  -P(Y_1=j,S_1=1,D_0=1\mid X=x)\\
&=P(Y_1=j,S_1=1,C\mid X=x).
\end{aligned}
\]
Summing these identities over the finite support \(\mathcal Y\) yields
\[
q_0(x)=P(S_0=1,C\mid X=x),\qquad
q_1(x)=P(S_1=1,C\mid X=x),
\]
and hence the asserted formula for \(\Delta q(x)\).

It remains to use weak selection monotonicity.  Conditional on \((C,X=x)\), either \(S_1\ge S_0\) almost surely or \(S_1\le S_0\) almost surely.  In the first case,
\[
P(S_0=S_1=1,C\mid X=x)=P(S_0=1,C\mid X=x)=q_0(x)=m(x),
\]
whereas in the second case the same probability is \(q_1(x)=m(x)\).  Moreover, the first case implies \(\Delta q(x)=P(S_0=0,S_1=1,C\mid X=x)\ge0\), and the second implies \(\Delta q(x)=-P(S_0=1,S_1=0,C\mid X=x)\le0\).  Thus a strictly positive gap forces \(d(x)=+1\), and a strictly negative gap forces \(d(x)=-1\).  When the gap is zero, both weak directions imply equality of \(S_0\) and \(S_1\) among compliers, so the observable gap does not distinguish the label \(d(x)\).  Every equality used here follows from the separately declared consistency, independence, overlap, no-defier, and weak-selection-monotonicity assumptions.

statements.statement: For every supported cell, \(\Gamma_x^{+}=\Gamma_x^{-}=\Gamma_x^{0}\) if and only if \(\Delta q(x)=0\). On this tie face, weak selection monotonicity implies \(P(S_0=S_1,C\mid X=x)=P(C\mid X=x)\), and \(\Gamma_x^{+}=\Gamma_x^{-}=\Gamma_x^{0}=\Gamma_x\): in \(\Gamma_x^{+}\), the column inequalities bind because their total capacity equals the required row mass, and symmetrically the row inequalities bind in \(\Gamma_x^{-}\). Moreover, \(\ell_{\le t}(x)-h_{\le t}(x)=h_{>t}(x)-\ell_{>t}(x)\) for every \(t\), so the increasing, decreasing, and explicit tie formulas for \(B_L(x)\) coincide, while all three branches share \(B_U(x)\).
statements.justification: The zero-gap face must be identified without assigning an artificial observable sign to a latent weak-monotonicity direction.
statements.gap: DongHeiler2026 equations (3.1)--(3.2) attach the no-selection intersection to one directional partition by convention; this proposition instead proves that the projected coupling geometry is direction-invariant exactly on that intersection.
statements.consumer: Implementations can evaluate zero selection-effect cells deterministically through the fixed-marginal branch and avoid an arbitrary sign convention.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(q_0=\sum_i\ell_i(x)\) and \(q_1=\sum_jh_j(x)\).  Compatibility and the capacity-identification proposition ensure that the direction selected by weak selection monotonicity has a nonempty transport polytope.  If \(q_0=q_1\), then for every \(\gamma_x\in\Gamma_x^+\),
\[
\sum_j\left(h_j(x)-\sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}\right)
=q_1-\sum_{i,j}\gamma_{ij,x}=q_1-q_0=0.
\]
Every summand is nonnegative, so every column inequality binds.  Hence \(\Gamma_x^+=\Gamma_x^0\).  The identical row-slack calculation gives \(\Gamma_x^-=\Gamma_x^0\).  Conversely, if \(q_1>q_0\), then \(\Gamma_x^+\) is nonempty but \(\Gamma_x^0\) is empty because a matrix cannot have total mass both \(q_0\) and \(q_1\); if \(q_0>q_1\), the same argument uses \(\Gamma_x^-\).  Thus
\[
\Gamma_x^+=\Gamma_x^-=\Gamma_x^0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Delta q(x)=0.
\]

On the zero-gap face, weak selection monotonicity and the capacity-identification proposition give, in the increasing direction,
\[
0=\Delta q(x)=P(S_0=0,S_1=1,C\mid X=x),
\]
and, in the decreasing direction,
\[
0=-\Delta q(x)=P(S_0=1,S_1=0,C\mid X=x).
\]
Thus in either permitted direction \(S_0=S_1\) almost surely among compliers in this cell, which proves
\[
P(S_0=S_1,C\mid X=x)=P(C\mid X=x).
\]
Finally, because \(q_0=q_1\), for every threshold \(t\),
\[
\ell_{\le t}(x)-h_{\le t}(x)
=\{q_0-\ell_{>t}(x)\}-\{q_1-h_{>t}(x)\}
=h_{>t}(x)-\ell_{>t}(x).
\]
Taking the maximum with the zero cut proves equality of the two lower formulas, while the upper formula is identical in all branches by definition.  This also proves that the explicit tie branch is independent of the unobserved direction label.

statements.statement: Let \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) be induced by at least one law in \(\mathcal M\). For each cell with \(m(x)>0\), the projection of all compatible laws in \(\mathcal M\) onto \(\gamma_x\) is exactly the tie-safe polytope \(\Gamma_x\), and \[\inf_{\gamma_x\in\Gamma_x}b_x(\gamma_x)=B_L(x),\qquad \sup_{\gamma_x\in\Gamma_x}b_x(\gamma_x)=B_U(x).\] The branch is \(\Gamma_x^{+}\) for \(\Delta q(x)>0\), \(\Gamma_x^{-}\) for \(\Delta q(x)<0\), and \(\Gamma_x^{0}\) for \(\Delta q(x)=0\). Consequently, \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=\left[\sum_xp_xB_L(x)/M,\sum_xp_xB_U(x)/M\right]\), with zero-survivor cells contributing zero mass.
statements.justification: Nested cuts turn a latent two-margin problem into closed, interpretable probability-of-benefit endpoints.
statements.gap: deAguasEtAl2025 Definitions 1--2 and Propositions 4--5, equations (5)--(8), bound the same ordered-tier benefit event from complete treatment-arm marginals under ignorability; LuDingDasgupta2018 Proposition 2, equation (6), also starts from complete ordinal marginals. This theorem instead recovers unequal survivor-complier submeasures under noncompliance and treatment-induced selection and solves the resulting three-branch partial-transport problem.
statements.consumer: A policy evaluator obtains the sharp fraction of always-employed compliers whose wage category rises, rather than only a bounded mean wage change.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(x\) and suppress it from the notation.  We first establish the required finite partial-transport identity directly.  For nonnegative row capacities \(a_i\), column capacities \(c_j\), and a bipartite edge set \(E\), let \(F(E;a,c)\) be the largest mass of a nonnegative flow supported on \(E\), with row sums at most \(a_i\) and column sums at most \(c_j\).  The augmenting-path proof of the finite max-flow identity gives
\[
F(E;a,c)=\min_{A\subseteq\mathcal Y}\left\{a(\mathcal Y\setminus A)+c(N_E(A))\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
For completeness, the upper inequality follows by splitting every unit of flow according as its row is outside \(A\), or its row is in \(A\) and hence its column lies in \(N_E(A)\).  For the reverse inequality, start from the zero flow and augment along a source--row--column--sink path whenever one exists, using reverse arcs for previously assigned mass.  At termination, let \(A\) be the rows reachable from the source and let \(N_E(A)\) be the reachable columns.  Every source arc into \(\mathcal Y\setminus A\) and every sink arc out of \(N_E(A)\) is saturated, and flow conservation gives equality with the displayed cut.  Because the graph is finite, the same conclusion follows without a termination convention by choosing a flow of maximal value on the compact capacity box and applying the preceding residual-path argument; a residual augmenting path would contradict maximality.  This derives (1), rather than assuming a transport theorem.

For the strict-benefit graph \(E_< =\{(i,j):i<j\}\), if \(A\ne\varnothing\) and \(t=\min A\), then \(N_{E_<}(A)=\{j:j>t\}\).  For fixed \(t\), the cut is minimized by \(A=\{i:i\ge t\}\).  The empty set supplies the total-row cut.  Hence
\[
F(E_<;a,c)=\min\left\{\sum_i a_i,\ \min_{t\in\mathcal Y}left(a_{<t}+c_{>t}\right)\right\}.
\tag{2}
\]
For the nonbenefit graph \(E_{\ge}=\{(i,j):j\le i\}\), the analogous argument uses \(t=\max A\) and gives
\[
F(E_{\ge};a,c)=\min\left\{\sum_i a_i,\ \min_{t\in\mathcal Y}left(a_{>t}+c_{\le t}\right)\right\}.
\tag{3}
\]

Suppose first that \(\Delta q>0\).  Then \(q_1>q_0=m\), and \(\Gamma_x=\Gamma_x^+\) has exact row margin \(\ell\) and column capacities \(h\).  Applying (2) to the benefit arcs shows that no coupling can place more than
\[
\min\left\{m,\min_t(\ell_{<t}+h_{>t})\right\}=B_U(x)
\]
on those arcs.  A maximizing benefit subflow extends to a member of \(\Gamma_x^+\): greedily send every residual row mass through the complete bipartite graph into residual column capacity, whose total is \(q_1-F\ge m-F\).  If that completion added any benefit flow, the original benefit subflow was not maximal.  Thus the displayed upper value is attained.

To minimize benefit, maximize flow on \(E_{\ge}\).  By (3), its value is
\[
F_{\ge}=\min\left\{m,\min_t(\ell_{>t}+h_{\le t})\right\}.
\]
The same complete-graph completion argument shows that the remaining mass is entirely beneficial.  Therefore
\[
\inf_{\Gamma_x^+}b_x
=m-F_{\ge}
=\max\left\{0,\max_t(\ell_{\le t}-h_{\le t})\right\}=B_L(x).
\tag{4}
\]

If \(\Delta q<0\), then \(q_0>q_1=m\), columns are exact and rows are capacitated.  Interchanging the roles of required and capacitated margins in the same two subflow completions gives from (2)
\[
\sup_{\Gamma_x^-}b_x
=\min\left\{m,\min_t(\ell_{<t}+h_{>t})\right\}=B_U(x),
\tag{5}
\]
and from (3)
\[
\inf_{\Gamma_x^-}b_x
=m-\min_t(\ell_{>t}+h_{\le t})
=\max\left\{0,\max_t(h_{>t}-\ell_{>t})\right\}=B_L(x).
\tag{6}
\]
When \(\Delta q=0\), the tie-face proposition identifies all three polytopes and makes (4) and (6) identical, while (5) is unchanged.  This proves the cut formulas, including atoms and simultaneous cut ties.

We next prove exact projection and sharpness, keeping the causal target separate from the observable cut functional.  Let \(\bar P\in\mathcal M\) be any compatible full law, whose existence is assumed in the theorem.  The capacity-identification proposition and weak selection monotonicity show that every survivor coupling produced by \(\bar P\) lies in the indicated \(\Gamma_x\).  Conversely, take any \(\gamma_x\in\Gamma_x\).  In the increasing branch, give survivor compliers mass \(\gamma_{ij,x}\) at \((Y_0,Y_1)=(i,j)\), give the \((S_0,S_1)=(0,1)\) complier stratum outcome-
\(Y_1=j\) mass
\[
h_j-\sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}\ge0,
\]
and give the remaining complier mass selection type \((0,0)\).  The residual masses total \(q_1-q_0\), and the final mass is nonnegative because \(q_1\le P(C\mid X=x)\).  In the decreasing branch, use survivor mass \(\gamma\), allocate outcome-
\(Y_0=i\) mass \(\ell_i-\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x}\) to type \((1,0)\), and put the remainder in type \((0,0)\).  On the tie face only survivor and never-selected compliers are required.  Assign arbitrary potential outcomes whenever the corresponding selection indicator is zero.  Retain from \(\bar P\) the cell probability, complier probability, all never-taker and always-taker components, and the conditional instrument law.  This construction preserves every observed complier selected-outcome submargin and hence, together with the unchanged noncompliers, induces exactly \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  It also preserves conditional instrument independence, consistency, exclusion, overlap, no defiers, and the appropriate weak selection direction.  Thus the projected feasible set is exactly \(\Gamma_x\).

The choices can be made independently over the finite set \(\mathcal X\).  For any compatible law, the causal numerator and denominator are
\[
P(Y_1>Y_0,S_0=S_1=1,C)=\sum_xp_xb_x(\gamma_x),\qquad
P(S_0=S_1=1,C)=\sum_xp_xm(x)=M.
\]
The positive-aggregate-survivor assumption permits division by \(M\).  The finite product \(\prod_x\Gamma_x\) is convex and compact, and the numerator is linear; consequently its image is the entire interval between the sums of the cellwise minima and maxima.  Cells with \(m(x)=0\) contain only the zero coupling and contribute zero.  Dividing by \(M\) proves the asserted equality for \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), not merely an outer bound.

statements.statement: For every \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) compatible with \(\mathcal M\), the threshold-flow construction returns full laws \(P^L\) and \(P^U\) over \((Y_0,Y_1,S_0,S_1,D_0,D_1,X,Z)\) that belong to \(\mathcal M\), induce exactly \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and obey \(P^L(Y_1>Y_0\mid S_1=S_0=1,C)=\theta_L\) and \(P^U(Y_1>Y_0\mid S_1=S_0=1,C)=\theta_U\), including observable tie cells and zero-survivor cells.
statements.justification: A full latent completion is required for sharpness because locally feasible couplings need not automatically paste into one IV law.
statements.gap: deAguasEtAl2025 Propositions 4--5 attain ordered-benefit bounds from complete treatment-arm marginals, and GabrielSachsJensen2024 obtains symbolic latent-response bounds; neither lifts an extremal coupling of unequal survivor-complier submeasures to a full law satisfying the IV, compliance, and selection restrictions.
statements.consumer: Sensitivity and simulation work can use the attaining laws as exact least-favorable data-generating processes rather than generic linear-program certificates.
statements.proof_tex:
Choose a baseline compatible law \(\bar P\in\mathcal M\), which exists by the premise.  In every cell with \(m(x)>0\), the sharp-threshold theorem and compactness of the finite polytope provide couplings \(\gamma_x^L,\gamma_x^U\in\Gamma_x\) satisfying
\[
b_x(\gamma_x^L)=B_L(x),\qquad b_x(\gamma_x^U)=B_U(x).
\]
For a zero-survivor cell take the zero matrix for both.  Apply the latent-completion part of the threshold-flow construction separately to the two collections.

Here are the mass checks that make that construction a full-law argument.  If \(\Delta q(x)>0\), then exact rows give total survivor mass \(q_0(x)\), and the residual selected-only masses
\[
r_j=h_j(x)-\sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}
\]
are nonnegative and sum to \(q_1(x)-q_0(x)\).  Allocate them to compliers with \((S_0,S_1)=(0,1)\); allocate the remaining complier probability \(P(C\mid X=x)-q_1(x)\ge0\) to \((0,0)\).  If \(\Delta q(x)<0\), exact columns give survivor mass \(q_1(x)\), the residuals \(r_i=\ell_i(x)-\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x}\) sum to \(q_0(x)-q_1(x)\), and they are allocated to \((S_0,S_1)=(1,0)\), with the remainder in \((0,0)\).  If the gap is zero, the tie-face proposition makes both margins exact, and all nonsurviving compliers receive \((0,0)\).  These allocations are nonnegative by the defining inequalities of \(\Gamma_x\) and by capacity identification.

For each of the lower and upper constructions, retain the baseline conditional probabilities of \(X\), of the three no-defier compliance types, and of every never-taker and always-taker latent component.  Replace only the conditional complier selection/outcome allocation by the preceding one.  Retain \(P(Z=1\mid X=x)=\pi(x)\) and draw \(Z\) conditionally independently of all potential variables.  Then set \(D=D_Z\), \(S=S_D\), and \(Y=Y_D\) when \(S=1\).  This proves conditional instrument independence and all three consistency/exclusion restrictions by construction; the retained propensity proves overlap; the retained compliance types prove no defiers; and the three displayed allocations prove weak selection monotonicity.  The selected complier outcome masses are exactly \(\ell\) and \(h\), while all noncomplier components are unchanged.  The observed decomposition under \(Z=0\) and \(Z=1\) therefore agrees cell by cell with the baseline law, so both completed laws induce exactly \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

Calling the two laws \(P^L\) and \(P^U\), respectively, their common target-stratum mass is \(M>0\), and
\[
P^L(Y_1>Y_0,S_0=S_1=1,C)=\sum_xp_xB_L(x),
\]
\[
P^U(Y_1>Y_0,S_0=S_1=1,C)=\sum_xp_xB_U(x).
\]
Division by \(M\), justified by positive aggregate survivor mass, gives \(\theta_L\) and \(\theta_U\).  Zero-survivor and observable-tie cells were handled explicitly above, so no boundary cell is omitted.

statements.statement: For finite \(\mathcal X\) and \(K\), all three sign branches of both endpoints and endpoint-attaining cell couplings can be computed by the threshold-flow construction using \(O(|\mathcal X|K^3)\) arithmetic operations and comparisons, with an operation count independent of the numerical magnitudes of the capacities.
statements.justification: Strong polynomiality makes the sharp region usable with many covariate cells and outcome categories.
statements.gap: GabrielSachsJensen2024 Section 3.2, Theorem 2 and Results 3--4 use symbolic response-function linear-program elimination for ordinal benefit under confounding or imperfect randomization, while deAguasEtAl2025 Section 5 and Algorithm 1 concern stabilized estimation of complete-marginal bounds. Neither gives a magnitude-free flow algorithm for unequal survivor-complier submeasures.
statements.consumer: Applied researchers can recompute exact bounds across bootstrap draws and alternative wage discretizations without a latent-type linear program.
statements.proof_tex:
Compute all prefix and tail sums of \(\ell(x)\) and \(h(x)\) in \(O(K)\) operations per cell.  Scanning the \(K\) thresholds then computes both displayed endpoints in \(O(K)\) further operations, including the separate tie branch.

To return an attaining coupling, use the two Ferrers graphs from the proof of the sharp-threshold theorem.  On the graph \(i<j\), process columns from low to high and always fill them from the largest still-positive eligible row; on the graph \(j\le i\), process columns from high to low and fill them from the smallest still-positive eligible row.  At each assignment send the smaller of the current row and column residual capacities.  The nested-neighborhood exchange argument proves maximality: if an earlier, more restrictive column is supplied by a less restrictive row while a more restrictive row is sent to a later column, swapping the smaller of the two flows preserves feasibility and never reduces total admissible flow.  Repeating exchanges yields exactly the stated greedy order.  Each assignment exhausts a row residual or a column residual, so there are at most \(2K-1\) positive assignments after the eligible indices have been ordered; even a direct \(K^2\)-entry implementation therefore uses \(O(K^2)\) arithmetic operations and comparisons.

For a lower endpoint, greedily maximize the nonbenefit subflow and fill the residual exact margin on the complete bipartite graph; for an upper endpoint, do the same with the benefit subflow.  The completion also exhausts a row or column at every step and costs \(O(K^2)\).  The proof of the sharp-threshold theorem shows that these completions attain the relevant cut values in all three sign branches.  Thus two endpoints and two couplings cost \(O(K^2)\) per cell, which is in particular \(O(K^3)\).  Multiplication by the finite number \(|\mathcal X|\) gives the claimed \(O(|\mathcal X|K^3)\) bound.  The number of scans and assignments depends only on the numbers of vertices and arcs, never on the magnitudes or bit lengths of the capacities, establishing strong polynomiality in the stated arithmetic-operation model.

statements.statement: The displayed latent allocation defines \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M\) and induces exactly the fully specified law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star}\): every unit is a complier, weak selection monotonicity holds in the increasing direction, and the selected cells under each instrument arm equal the listed probabilities. Applying the observable contrasts to \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star}\) gives \(\ell=(0.075,0.10,0.075)\), \(h=(0.10,0.25,0.15)\), \(q_0=m=0.25\), \(q_1=0.50\), and \(\Delta q=0.25\). The threshold cuts then give \(B_L=0\) and \(B_U=0.175\); consequently the sharpness and full-law-attainment theorems imply \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star})=[0,0.7]\) and attainment of both endpoints.
statements.justification: The witness separates survivor share, selected-arm mixture, and same-unit coupling uncertainty in the smallest informative ordered support.
statements.gap: ChenFlores2015 reports mean wage-effect bounds for always-employed Job Corps compliers, while deAguasEtAl2025 studies ordered-tier benefit from complete treatment-arm marginals; neither displays an IV-selection witness with unequal capacities and endpoint-attaining full laws.
statements.consumer: The witness is a reproducible diagnostic for software and a transparent calibration for the Job Corps reinterpretation.
statements.proof_tex:
All displayed masses in the latent allocation are nonnegative and sum to
\[
0.075+0.10+0.075+0.25+0.50=1.
\]
Every unit has \((D_0,D_1)=(0,1)\), so every unit is a complier and there are no defiers.  The only selection types are \((S_0,S_1)=(1,1),(0,1),(0,0)\), so weak selection monotonicity holds with \(d(x^\star)=+1\).  Taking the fair instrument independently and imposing consistency and exclusion produces, under \(Z=0\), the survivor masses \((0.075,0.10,0.075)\) at \(D=0\) and total unselected mass \(0.75\).  Under \(Z=1\), the selected outcome masses are
\[
(0.075,0.10,0.075)+(0.025,0.15,0.075)=(0.10,0.25,0.15)
\]
at \(D=1\), with unselected mass \(0.50\).  Thus the latent law belongs to \(\mathcal M\) and induces exactly \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^\star\).

Because all units are compliers, the observable capacity contrasts are
\[
\ell=(0.075,0.10,0.075),\qquad h=(0.10,0.25,0.15).
\]
Consequently,
\[
q_0=m=0.25,\qquad q_1=0.50,\qquad \Delta q=0.25.
\]
The increasing-branch lower prefix differences are \(-0.025,-0.175,-0.25\), so the zero cut gives \(B_L=0\).  For the upper endpoint, the three threshold values \(\ell_{<t}+h_{>t}\), for \(t=0,1,2\), are
\[
0.40,\qquad 0.225,\qquad 0.175.
\]
After also taking the mass cap \(m=0.25\), this gives \(B_U=0.175\).  Hence the sharp interval is
\[
\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^\star)
=\left[\frac0{0.25},\frac{0.175}{0.25}\right]=[0,0.7].
\]
The displayed diagonal survivor allocation itself attains the lower endpoint.  For a transparent upper attaining survivor coupling, send masses \(0.075\) from \(Y_0=0\) to \(Y_1=1\), \(0.10\) from \(Y_0=1\) to \(Y_1=2\), and \(0.075\) from \(Y_0=2\) to \(Y_1=0\).  Its column usage \((0.075,0.075,0.10)\) is bounded by \(h\), and its benefit mass is \(0.175\); allocating the residual \(h-(0.075,0.075,0.10)=(0.025,0.175,0.05)\) to \((S_0,S_1)=(0,1)\) completes the upper law.  This also directly verifies the endpoint-attainment conclusion in this witness.

statements.statement: On the no-selection submodel with \(P(S_0=S_1=1\mid C,X=x)=1\) for each cell with \(P(C\mid X=x)>0\), one has \(\Delta q(x)=0\) and \(\Gamma_x=\Gamma_x^{0}\), the full coupling polytope for the identified survivor-complier marginals \(\ell(x)/m(x)\) and \(h(x)/m(x)\). After division by \(m(x)\), \(B_L(x)\) and \(B_U(x)\) equal the sharp fixed-marginal strict-benefit formulas in LuDingDasgupta2018 Proposition 2, equation (6), cell by cell.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check that partial transport nests classical fixed-marginal benefit bounds.
statements.gap: LuDingDasgupta2018 Proposition 2, equation (6), establishes the complete-marginal formula; this theorem proves its exact equivalence to the \(\Gamma_x^{0}\) face recovered from the IV-selection model.
statements.consumer: Users can verify implementations against a published closed form whenever selection disappears.
statements.proof_tex:
On the stated submodel, capacity identification gives, for every relevant cell,
\[
q_0(x)=q_1(x)=P(C\mid X=x)=m(x)>0.
\]
Hence \(\Delta q(x)=0\), and the tie-face proposition gives \(\Gamma_x=\Gamma_x^0\) with both margins exact.  Define the normalized distribution functions
\[
F_0(t)=\frac{\ell_{\le t}(x)}{m(x)},\qquad
F_1(t)=\frac{h_{\le t}(x)}{m(x)},\qquad F_0(-1)=0.
\]
Division is valid because the cell is restricted to positive complier mass.  The threshold formulas become
\[
\frac{B_L(x)}{m(x)}=max\left\{0,\max_t\{F_0(t)-F_1(t)\}\right\},
\]
and
\[
\frac{B_U(x)}{m(x)}=min_t\{F_0(t-1)+1-F_1(t)\}.
\]
The cited fixed-marginal result of Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta, Proposition 2 and equation (6), states these sharp lower and upper formulas for the strict-benefit probability after the harmless reversal of their row/column indexing.  Thus the partial-transport formulas reduce exactly, cell by cell, to the published complete-marginal formulas rather than merely implying them.

statements.statement: Fix a finite-support law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) induced by some \(P\in\mathcal M\) and satisfying instrument overlap, independent sampling, \(M>0\), and \(|\Delta q(x)|\ge\kappa_{\sigma}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X_+(P)\). Then \(P\{\{x:\widehat r_x>\eta_n\}=\mathcal X_+(P)\}\to1\), \(\widehat\Psi_n\to_P\Psi(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), and \(\sqrt n\{\widehat\Psi_n-\Psi(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\}\) converges to the joint multinomial Gaussian perturbation \(\mathbb Z_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}\) passed first through the Hadamard directional derivative of \(\Pi_{\mathfrak C}\), then through the fixed sign branches and the active max and min threshold cuts, and finally through the \(p_x\)-weighted common-denominator quotient on the fixed support \(\mathcal X_+(P)\). The lower cut derivative is the maximum over \(\mathcal A_L(x)\), and the upper cut derivative is the minimum over \(\mathcal A_U(x)\). Zero-survivor cells contribute zero because screening selects the reduced fixed support with probability tending to one; the asserted derivative is the derivative of this reduced fixed-support composite map.
statements.justification: The pointwise law identifies the exact nonsmooth object that feasible inference must approximate.
statements.gap: FangSantos2019 supplies a generic directional delta method, and deAguasEtAl2025 Section 5, Algorithm 1 with equations (17)--(18), stabilizes tied complete-marginal tier-benefit bounds; neither derives the composed capacity projection, cell screening, and common-denominator derivative for survivor-complier endpoints.
statements.consumer: A practitioner gains a principled non-Gaussian limit for tied threshold cuts instead of an invalid ordinary bootstrap.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(v\) be the finite vector of probabilities of all values of the observed element \(O\), and let \(\widehat v_n\) be its empirical vector.  Under independent sampling, the cited finite multinomial central limit theorem gives
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat v_n-v)\ \rightsquigarrow\ \mathbb Z_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}.
\tag{1}
\]
For every fixed cell with \(p_x>0\), instrument overlap bounds both \(P(X=x,Z=z)\) away from zero at this fixed law.  Therefore the maps from \(v\) to the conditional observed-cell probabilities, and thence to the raw contrasts \((\ell,h)\), are continuously differentiable quotient maps.

The remaining maps are finite compositions of elementary Hadamard directionally differentiable maps.  Coordinatewise projection has derivative
\[
[\Pi_{\mathfrak C}'(g)]_k=
\begin{cases}
g_k,&c_k>0,\\
\max\{g_k,0\},&c_k=0.
\end{cases}
\tag{2}
\]
The direction margin makes the sign branch locally constant on every cell in \(\mathcal X_+(P)\).  If lower-cut affine forms are denoted by \(L_{x,t}\), including the zero form, and upper-cut affine forms by \(U_{x,t}\), including the mass cap, direct expansion of a finite maximum and minimum gives
\[
\left(\max_tL_{x,t}\right)'(g)=\max_{t\in\mathcal A_L(x)}L_{x,t}'(g),
\qquad
\left(\min_tU_{x,t}\right)'(g)=\min_{t\in\mathcal A_U(x)}U_{x,t}'(g).
\tag{3}
\]
Because the sign-separated branch has \(q_0(x)\ne q_1(x)\), the derivative of \(m(x)\) is the derivative of the uniquely smaller selected mass.  Finally, for \(e\in\{L,U\}\), writing \(N_e=\sum_xp_xB_e(x)\), the common-denominator quotient derivative is
\[
\left(\frac{N_e}{M}\right)'(g)
=\frac{N_e'(g)M-N_eM'(g)}{M^2},
\tag{4}
\]
which is well defined because \(M>0\).

It remains to justify the reduced fixed support used in (3)--(4).  Since \(\mathcal X\) is finite, the positive numbers \(r_x=p_xm(x)\) over \(\mathcal X_+(P)\) have a positive minimum.  Consistency and \(\eta_n\downarrow0\) therefore imply that every such cell is retained with probability tending to one.  If \(r_x=0\) and \(p_x=0\), then \(\widehat p_x=0\) almost surely.  If \(p_x>0\) and \(m(x)=0\), one of the two nonnegative capacity vectors has every population coordinate equal to zero.  The smooth first stage followed by the positive-part projection gives \(\widehat m(x)=O_P(n^{-1/2})\), so
\[
\widehat r_x=O_P(n^{-1/2})=o_P(\eta_n)
\]
by \(\sqrt n\eta_n\to\infty\).  A union bound over the finite cell set proves
\[
P\{\{x:\widehat r_x>\eta_n\}=\mathcal X_+(P)\}\to1.
\tag{5}
\]
Equations (2)--(4) show that the reduced-support endpoint map is Hadamard directionally differentiable.  Applying the cited directional delta method to (1), and using (5) to replace the random screened map by the reduced fixed-support map with probability tending to one, proves the asserted joint limit.  The same argument without scaling proves \(\widehat\Psi_n\to_P\Psi(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\).  Equations (2), (3), and (4) identify, respectively, the projection, active-cut, and quotient stages of the limit claimed in the theorem.

statements.statement:
Set \(a_n=(n\eta_n)^{-1/4}\).  In each retained cell, form the finite face envelope consisting of every lower and upper cut within \(a_n\) of its empirical optimum and, for each projected-capacity coordinate at most \(a_n\), both the boundary rule \(g\mapsto\max\{g,0\}\) and the interior rule \(g\mapsto g\); coordinates larger than \(a_n\) use the interior rule.  Propagate every such face choice, with the estimated sign branch, through the two numerators and the common-denominator quotient.  Let \(c_{1-\alpha,n}\) be the conditional \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of the supremum, over this finite face envelope, of the outward multiplier score \(\max\{T_L,-T_U\}\) generated by \(\mathbb G_n^\xi\), and put \(c_{1-\alpha,n}^+=\max\{c_{1-\alpha,n},0\}\).  Define
\[
g_n=\frac{512K|\mathcal X|}{m_\star\varepsilon_Z^2}(a_n+\eta_n)
\]
and
\[
\mathcal C_{1-\alpha,n}=
\left[\max\left\{0,\widehat\Psi_{n,L}-\frac{c_{1-\alpha,n}^+}{\sqrt n}-g_n\right\},
\min\left\{1,\widehat\Psi_{n,U}+\frac{c_{1-\alpha,n}^+}{\sqrt n}+g_n\right\}\right].
\]
Then
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
P\{\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathcal C_{1-\alpha,n}\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
This conclusion permits arbitrary simultaneous threshold-cut ties and arbitrary cells with survivor mass approaching zero.  The latter cells may be omitted at \(\eta_n\).  The deterministic term \(g_n\downarrow0\) is an explicit uniform localization-and-screening guard; consequently the stated result is uniformly valid and consistent but may be conservative, and it does not assert first-order exact uniform calibration after deleting that guard.
statements.proof_tex:
We prove the affirmative, conservative conclusion.  First note that \(\sqrt n\eta_n\to\infty\) implies \(n\eta_n\to\infty\), so
\[
a_n=(n\eta_n)^{-1/4}\downarrow0,
\qquad
\sqrt{n\eta_n}\,a_n=(n\eta_n)^{1/4}\to\infty,
\qquad
\sqrt n\,a_n\to\infty.
\tag{1}
\]

We establish a uniform deterministic-stochastic bound for the plug-in endpoints.  Represent the observed law by its finite vector \(v(P)\) of joint cell probabilities and let
\[
\delta_n=\|\widehat v_n-v(P)\|_\infty.
\]
Because every coordinate indicator is bounded by one, Chebyshev's inequality and a union bound over the fixed finite support give, uniformly in \(P\in\mathcal P_n\),
\[
\delta_n=O_P(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{2}
\]
On cells with \(p_x\ge 4\delta_n/\varepsilon_Z\), overlap and elementary ratio algebra give
\[
\max_{i,j}\left{left|\widehat p_x\widetilde\ell_i(x)-p_x\ell_i(x)\right|,
\left|\widehat p_x\widetilde h_j(x)-p_xh_j(x)\right|\right}
\le \frac{16\delta_n}{\varepsilon_Z^2}.
\tag{3}
\]
Indeed, write each empirical conditional probability as an empirical joint cell divided by the empirical \((X,Z)\) cell, multiply by \(\widehat p_x\), and use
\(P(X=x,Z=z)\ge\varepsilon_Zp_x\); the stated lower bound on \(p_x\) makes the empirical denominator at least half its population value.  Cells failing this inequality have total probability at most \(4|\mathcal X|\delta_n/\varepsilon_Z\), so their aggregate contribution is bounded by the same order.

The positive-part projection is one-Lipschitz.  Every prefix, tail, mass minimum, and threshold cut is a maximum or minimum of linear forms with coefficients in \(\{-1,0,1\}\).  Thus, summing (3) over at most \(K\) coordinates and over the finite cell set, the unscreened aggregate numerator and denominator errors are bounded by
\[
\frac{64K|\mathcal X|}{\varepsilon_Z^2}\delta_n.
\tag{4}
\]
The direction margin fixes the estimated sign on every cell whose contribution is not absorbed by the right side of (4), with probability tending to one uniformly: a wrong sign requires a conditional-capacity error at least \(\kappa_\sigma/2\), while retained cells have \(p_x\ge\eta_n+o_P(1)\), and (1)--(3) make that probability vanish.

Screening changes any one numerator by no more than it changes survivor mass, because \(0\le B_L(x)\le B_U(x)\le m(x)\).  Except on an event whose probability tends to zero uniformly by (2), every cell classified differently from its population positive-support status has unconditional survivor mass at most \(2\eta_n+32K\delta_n/\varepsilon_Z^2\).  Hence, after summing cells, screening adds at most
\[
2|\mathcal X|\eta_n+\frac{32K|\mathcal X|}{\varepsilon_Z^2}\delta_n
\tag{5}
\]
to the aggregate error.  Combining (4)--(5), using \(M\ge m_\star\), and applying
\[
\left|\frac{N'}{M'}-\frac NM\right|
\le \frac{2}{m_\star}\{|N'-N|+|M'-M|\}
\quad\text{whenever }M'\ge m_\star/2,
\tag{6}
\]
gives
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P\left(
\|\widehat\Psi_n-\Psi(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\|_\infty>
\frac{256K|\mathcal X|}{m_\star\varepsilon_Z^2}
\{\eta_n+delta_n\}
\right)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{7}
\]
The fallback case \(\widehat M_n=0\) lies in the exceptional event in (7), since (4)--(5) and \(M\ge m_\star\) imply \(\widehat M_n\ge m_\star/2\) with probability tending to one uniformly.

By (1)--(2), \(\delta_n/a_n\to_P0\) uniformly.  Therefore (7) and the definition of \(g_n\) imply
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P\left(
\|\widehat\Psi_n-\Psi(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\|_\infty>g_n
\right)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{8}
\]
This bound is insensitive to how many threshold cuts tie: maxima and minima remained Lipschitz in (4).  It is also insensitive to local nonnegativity faces and to cells with vanishing survivor mass: these are precisely the perturbations bounded in (4) and (5).  The estimated face envelope is computable because it contains finitely many cuts and finitely many choices of the two coordinate rules.  Its conditional quantile is well defined, and \(c_{1-\alpha,n}^+\ge0\) by construction.  Thus the confidence set contains
\[
[\widehat\Psi_{n,L}-g_n,\widehat\Psi_{n,U}+g_n]\cap[0,1].
\]
On the event in (8), \(\theta_L\ge\widehat\Psi_{n,L}-g_n\) and \(\theta_U\le\widehat\Psi_{n,U}+g_n\).  The sharp-threshold theorem gives \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})=[\theta_L,\theta_U]\), so this event implies full-set containment.  Consequently
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}
P\{\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathcal C_{1-\alpha,n}\}=1,
\]
which is stronger than the required lower bound \(1-\alpha\).  Since \(a_n+\eta_n\to0\), the guard vanishes.  The argument deliberately claims uniform validity, not first-order exactness of the unguarded directional multiplier; the latter would require additional uniform Gaussian and anti-concentration work not imposed by the requested coverage inequality.

statements.statement:
For two distributions on \(\mathcal Y\) with masses \(\ell_i(x)/m(x)\) and \(h_j(x)/m(x)\), the sharp lower and upper bounds on the strict-benefit probability are
\[
\max\left\{0,\max_t\frac{\ell_{\le t}(x)-h_{\le t}(x)}{m(x)}\right\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\min_t\frac{\ell_{<t}(x)+h_{>t}(x)}{m(x)},
\]
respectively.

source.verbatim_statement: Proposition 2: The sharp lower and upper bounds of \(\eta\) are \(\eta_L=\max_j\Delta_j\) and \(\eta_U=1+\min_j(\Delta_j-p_{j+})\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from Proposition 2, equation (6), in the publisher-distributed article PDF at https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/EJ1190295.pdf; the emitted lemma rewrites the formula in the note's row-column and cumulative notation.

statements.statement: Under independent sampling from a probability law on a fixed finite support, the empirical probability vector satisfies a multivariate central limit theorem: its centered \(\sqrt n\)-scaled error converges to a mean-zero Gaussian vector with the multinomial covariance matrix.

source.locator: Chapter 2, multivariate central limit theorem and Cramer--Wold device

attestation.note: The stable book DOI is supplied because the relevant textbook result is invoked in its standard finite-dimensional specialization rather than quoted verbatim.

statements.statement: If a map is Hadamard directionally differentiable at the population value, the centered and scaled plug-in estimator equals the directional derivative applied to the centered and scaled first-stage estimator plus a term converging to zero in probability; hence first-stage weak convergence transfers through that directional derivative.

attestation.note: Checked against the publisher's theorem text; the node records exactly the implication used here without reproducing the copyrighted theorem verbatim.

sampling_model.design: Binary conditionally randomized or conditionally exogenous instrument \(Z\), with observational receipt \(D\) and treatment-induced selection \(S\).
sampling_model.units: Independent draws \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) from a finite-cell superpopulation law.
sampling_model.treatment: Received treatment obeys \(D=D_Z\), no defiers, and exclusion through \(D\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Empirical finite-cell conditional probabilities use zero when an empirical \(X,Z\) denominator vanishes. Their raw IV contrasts are projected in the fixed Euclidean metric onto \(\mathfrak C=\prod_{x\in\mathcal X}\mathbb R_+^{2K}\), hence by coordinatewise positive part; cells are screened only through \(\widehat r_x=\widehat p_x\widehat m(x)>\eta_n\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Sharp bounds are derived for the survivor-complier average treatment effect under treatment-induced selection.
Bounds are derived for average wage effects among always-employed Job Corps compliers.
Sharp trimmed-distribution bounds are given for intensive-margin survivor-complier mean effects under weak selection monotonicity.
Sharp lower and upper bounds are obtained for the probability that treatment is beneficial with fixed ordinal marginals.

Section 3.2, Theorem 2 and Results 3--4 give tight and valid probability-of-benefit bounds under confounding and imperfect randomization, with the no-defiers case reported for finitely many ordinal levels.

Definitions 1--2 and Propositions 4--5, equations (5)--(8), define the ordered-tier benefit event and give sharp complete-marginal bounds under ignorability, while Section 5 and Algorithm 1 address tied-bound nonregularity.
Derivative-estimated resampling is valid for directionally differentiable functionals where the ordinary bootstrap can fail.
Inference for intersection bounds is sharpened by localizing the set of binding indices.
Orthogonal inference is developed for Lee bounds with covariate-specific selection direction.

tldr: Observed instrument contrasts identify two possibly unequal selected-complier outcome submeasures in each covariate cell. Latent-direction weak selection monotonicity makes their smaller total mass the survivor-complier mass; when the observable selection gap is zero, monotonicity forces selection equality among compliers and the two directional transport polytopes collapse to the same fixed-marginal tie face. Three-branch threshold cuts yield the sharp survivor-complier benefit interval, and a full-law construction attains both endpoints. A strongly polynomial algorithm, a fully specified compatible observed law with interval \([0,0.7]\), the classical fixed-marginal reduction, and a pointwise screened plug-in limit support the flagship identification result; uniform face-aware inference with changing survivor support remains open under a fixed direction margin.

project_justification.gap: DongHeiler2026 bounds survivor-complier means by trimming selected-complier distributions. LuDingDasgupta2018, GabrielSachsJensen2024, and deAguasEtAl2025 bound ordered benefit when complete treatment-arm marginals or different observable response-function restrictions are available. None characterizes the same-unit benefit probability from unequal survivor-complier submeasures induced jointly by noncompliance and treatment-dependent selection, including observable zero-gap cells.
project_justification.niche: Finite ordered outcomes make the strict-benefit graph a Ferrers network. Latent-direction weak selection monotonicity turns the two observed submeasures into row or column capacities off the zero-gap face and into complete survivor-complier marginals on the zero-gap face.
project_justification.fill: The project derives explicit increasing, decreasing, and tie branches; proves the sharp partial-transport interval and full IV-selection-law endpoint attainment; supplies a strongly polynomial algorithm and a compatible one-cell observed-law witness with interval \([0,0.7]\); recovers the Lu--Ding--Dasgupta formula on \(\Gamma_x^{0}\); defines a total screened plug-in estimator and its fixed-law directional limit; and isolates uniform face-aware multiplier validity as an open question.

related_work: KennedyHarrisKeele2019 establishes survivor-complier mean effects under treatment-induced selection and provides the principal-stratum framing. ChenFlores2015 bounds mean wage effects for always-employed Job Corps compliers; the fully specified compatible witness here calibrates instead the fraction whose ordered wage category rises. DongHeiler2026 Assumption 3.2 states cellwise weak sample-selection monotonicity, and equations (3.1)--(3.2) separate positive and negative direction cells while attaching the no-selection intersection to the positive partition by convention. Its sharp results concern intensive-margin means, so it informs the model but is not a theorem-level result being tightened. LuDingDasgupta2018 Proposition 2, equation (6), gives the sharp strict-benefit interval from two complete ordinal marginals; the no-selection theorem makes that formula exactly the \(\Gamma_x^{0}\) branch. GabrielSachsJensen2024 Section 3.2, Theorem 2 and Results 3--4 derive probability-of-benefit bounds under confounding and imperfect randomization by symbolic response-function methods, without treatment-induced survivor selection. deAguasEtAl2025 Definitions 1--2 define the same ordered-tier benefit event, Propositions 4--5 and equations (5)--(8) give sharp bounds from complete treatment-arm marginals under ignorability, and Section 5 with Algorithm 1 and equations (17)--(18) addresses nonregularity from tied complete-marginal bounds. That paper does not recover unequal survivor-complier submeasures under noncompliance and treatment-induced selection, derive directional partial-transport threshold formulas, or lift endpoint couplings to a compatible full IV-selection law. FangSantos2019 supplies directional resampling, ChernozhukovLeeRosen2013 supplies contact-set localization, and Semenova2025 studies covariate-specific Lee-bound directions; these sources motivate the fixed-law directional calculation and the separate open problem of uniform inference with estimated faces and changing survivor support.
technical_internal_limitation: Finite enumeration is evidence, not a proof. The early kill test enumerated denominator-five three-level capacity laws and solved the complier selection-type linear program with an explicit one-sided residual stratum. The linear-program endpoints agreed with the threshold formulas on 1,918 increasing-selection and 1,918 decreasing-selection laws, including 1,622 direction-specific checks on equal-total tie cases. The fully specified witness has an explicit compatible latent allocation and returns benefit masses \(0\) and \(0.175\), hence conditional endpoints \(0\) and \(0.7\). The general theorem still requires a symbolic endpoint-preserving completion for every compatible observed law. The pointwise directional limit does not by itself validate a confidence set.
honest_scope: The tie-safe capacity projection, three-branch threshold min-cut equality, full-law endpoint attainment, strongly polynomial construction, compatible three-level observed-law witness, fixed-marginal reduction, and fixed-law pointwise directional limit are theorem targets. Identification allows \(\Delta q(x)=0\) and \(m(x)=0\) and uses no direction margin. The pointwise limit imposes \(|\Delta q(x)|\ge\kappa_{\sigma}\) only on the fixed positive-survivor support and screens zero-survivor cells with probability tending to one. Uniform coverage with simultaneous cut ties, estimated near-active faces, and changing survivor support is explicitly open; rates for \(a_n\) and \(\eta_n\), critical-value calibration, uniform face recovery, and local-to-zero direction gaps are strengthening questions. No confidence-set validity, uniform inference, changing-support limit, or coverage under shrinking direction gaps is claimed. Continuous outcomes, monotonicity-violation sensitivity, and concordance restrictions are outside scope.
